A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ISF and Thinking-in-Substructures study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite renumbering and added sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original Transformer and LLM experiments, including synthetic substructure extraction, Tins comparisons, and molecular functional-group extraction in Tables 1–4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds accuracy-versus-training-epoch results comparing adjacency-list and edge-list representations in Appendix E.3, Table 8.

M1.justification: The Transformer architecture, ISF construction, Tins decomposition and answer sequence, and attributed-graph encoding remain unchanged. Renamed extraction settings clarify existing procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic graph tasks, LLM extraction and concept-learning scenarios, and QM9/PCBA functional-group datasets. The added epoch analysis revisits square and pentagon extraction without expanding task or data coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain unchanged, including AL versus EL and direct prediction versus Tins. v2 Table 5 compares model families conceptually; it does not introduce evaluated GNN or graph-Transformer baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds an epoch-dependent evaluation using four-layer models for squares and five-layer models for pentagons, with reported checkpoints from 10,000 to 60,000 epochs. This supplements the existing depth comparison rather than establishing revisions to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix E.3 and Table 8 add a training-budget sensitivity analysis testing whether EL's disadvantage persists with longer training. Existing prompt perturbations, layer visualizations, and other analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Three-run averaging for Table 1 and existing uncertainty reporting are retained. Table 8 adds ± values, but neither it nor the new checklist specifies new run counts, seeds, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 Table 8 adds epoch-specific accuracies: for example, pentagon extraction reaches 0.92 ± 0.004 with AL at 40,000 epochs and 0.93 ± 0.044 with EL at 60,000 epochs. These are newly reported results under different budgets; existing benchmark values and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The bounds, assumptions, and proofs in v1 Appendix A are retained in v2 Appendix D. New Definitions 3.7 and 3.9 restate extraction objectives already expressed in v1 Theorems 3.7–3.8; renaming and revised cross-references do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about ISF, its consistency with LLM behavior, Tins, and attributed-graph extraction. Added supporting discussion does not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix E.3 qualifies the AL/EL comparison by explaining that EL learns less efficiently but eventually reaches comparable accuracy. New appendices also discuss potential applications beyond graphs and acknowledge the focus on extraction fundamentals and omitted theoretical detail.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link on the first page and discloses in Appendix E.3 that the existing AL/EL results selected the epoch where AL performed best. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, data construction, and splits remain documented as before.

R1.justification: New Appendix C and Table 5 position decoder-only Transformers against GNNs and graph Transformers through their inputs, outputs, and learning mechanisms. Three references are added: Chen et al. on substructure counting, Müller et al. on principled graph Transformers, and Zhu et al. on structural expressive power.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies task terminology and visualization labels, renames Sections 4–5, and adds short appendices, acknowledgments, and a checklist. Most prose remains intact. Several cross-references now incorrectly call definitions, assumptions, or lemmas 'Theorem'.

P2.justification: v2 adds the conceptual comparison table and epoch-results table, expands Figure 2's caption, and reflows and renumbers appendix material. Existing figure images and the structure of retained result tables are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added epoch analysis and disclosure of AL-based epoch selection make the representation comparison easier to assess. Clearer task descriptions and code-access information provide modest additional value, outweighing new cross-reference mistakes and unfinished revision wording in Appendix E.3.
